followup_reason: Diagnosis (no formal model; all fabricated equation fields cleared) rests on the original being a pre-1990 scanned-image paper not machine-readable via web fetch. editor_summary: Editor 1 and both reviewers unanimously agree (accept). The original fields are fabricated cross-contamination from VI-scheduling/molar-maximizing and incremental-learning frameworks: a fictitious "Relative Duration" RD=log(X/Y) predictor, an "expected lock-up time" L=X^2/2I VI reinforcement-loss construct with a %lost=100*L/(X+Y) metric, and a 1/n_t delta-rule recursion. None of these correspond to anything in Stein, Sidman & Brady (1958), a descriptive conditioned-suppression (CER) experiment that presents no formal quantitative model or displayed governing equation. The canonical suppression ratio B/(B+A) postdates this paper (Annau & Kamin, 1961) and is a measure rather than a model, so it is correctly not retrofitted. All equation fields are cleared to the empty set, which faithfully represents the paper. changed=true because the fabricated fields were removed. signoffs=0 and human_followup_required=true because the empty-set conclusion depends on confirming, against the scanned (non-machine-readable) original, that no equation or incidental displayed metric was reported.

final_static_definitions: Y = avoidance response rate (responses per unit time); X = the temporal parameter that was varied simultaneously and equally (the shock-shock and response-shock intervals of the Sidman free-operant avoidance procedure); 274.3 = empirically fitted constant; -1.1104 = empirically fitted exponent of the power-function regression. Equivalently log Y = log(274.3) - 1.1104 log X. NOTE: the surviving fragment 'Y=274.3X-1.1104' is genuinely ambiguous and is also readable as an ordinary linear regression Y = 274.3 X - 1.1104 (slope 274.3, intercept -1.1104); the power form is the more defensible reading (a negative exponent yields rate decreasing as the interval lengthens, consistent with avoidance) but cannot be confirmed against the scanned 1959 page image.
final_recursive_definitions: Y = avoidance response rate (responses per unit time); X = the simultaneously and equally varied temporal parameter (shock-shock and response-shock intervals); 274.3 = fitted constant; -1.1104 = fitted exponent. This recursive field is a DUPLICATE of the static field: the catalog carried the single empirical equation across both fields rather than presenting two distinct models. Same linear-alternative caveat applies (Y = 274.3 X - 1.1104).

final_static_definitions: I is the index of curvature; the fixed interval is divided into 4 equal parts (quarters). R_4 is the total (cumulative) number of responses emitted during the interval; R_1, R_2, R_3 are the cumulative numbers of responses emitted by the end of the first, second, and third quarters, respectively. The index equals the normalized area between the cumulative-response curve and the constant-rate diagonal. A constant response rate yields I = 0; positive values indicate positively accelerated (FI-scalloped) responding concentrated near the end of the interval, negative values indicate front-loaded responding. For n = 4 the index is bounded by -3/8 and +3/8 (i.e. ±(n-1)/2n), reaching +3/8 = 0.375 when all responding occurs at the very end of the interval.
final_recursive_definitions: I is the index of curvature; n is the number of equal parts into which the fixed interval is divided; R_n is the total (cumulative) number of responses emitted during the interval; R_i (i = 1, 2, ..., n-1) is the cumulative number of responses emitted by the end of the i-th part. The index equals the normalized area between the cumulative-response curve and the constant-rate diagonal. It is 0 for a constant response rate, increases toward +(n-1)/2n (approaching +0.5 as n increases) as responding becomes concentrated near the end of the interval, and decreases toward -(n-1)/2n for front-loaded responding.
followup_reason: Reviewers materially disagreed on a factor-of-2 in the normalizing denominator (Reviewer 1 reject: 2nR_n / 8R_4; Reviewer 2 accept and Editor 1: nR_n / 4R_4). The senior-editor decision adopts the 2nR_n normalization because the index of curvature is, by definition, the normalized area between the cumulative-response curve and the constant-rate diagonal, which forces the denominator 2nR_n and reproduces the canonical, widely cited range of ±(n-1)/2n (max 0.375 for n=4, approaching ±0.5), consistent with empirically reported FI-scallop values. However, this OVERRIDES the literal corrupted-OCR fragments, which both show 4R_4 / nR_n with no surviving leading coefficient 2, and Reviewer 2's two-distinct-token argument (4R_4 vs 3R_4 in the static fragment) is non-trivial. The 1960 JEAB paper is a scanned, non-machine-readable image and the CURVAT restatement (Springer) is behind an auth wall; web/secondary sources could not be machine-read to display the printed denominator. The literal printed normalizer must be confirmed against the physical/scanned 1960 page before signoff.
editor_summary: Index 117 (Fry, Kelleher & Cook, 1960, "A mathematical index of performance on fixed-interval schedules"). The two corrupted fragments are the n=4 worked case and its n-part generalization of the index of curvature; both lost their fraction bars. Editor 1 and Reviewer 2 reconstructed denominator nR_n (4R_4); Reviewer 1 rejected, arguing the denominator must be 2nR_n (8R_4) to yield the canonical ±(n-1)/2n ≈ ±0.5 range. As senior editor I side with Reviewer 1 on the substance: the index is by construction the normalized area between the cumulative curve and the constant-rate diagonal, which I derived independently as [(n-1)R_n - 2ΣR_i]/(2nR_n); this gives I=0 at constant rate, max (n-1)/2n = 0.375 at n=4, and matches the empirically observed FI-scallop ceiling (~0.5), whereas nR_n implies an uncited 0.75 ceiling and doubles every value. Final fields therefore use denominators 8R_4 and 2nR_n with corrected range statements and supplied definitions (previously empty). changed=true. I withhold signoff (signoffs=0) and flag human follow-up: the correction overrides the literal OCR tokens (4R_4 / nR_n), one reviewer accepted the uncorrected form, and the printed denominator can only be confirmed against the scanned 1960 page, which was not machine-readable.

final_static_definitions: Response Units = extinction output expressed in reinforcement-schedule units (number of reinforcement-equivalent response clusters emitted during extinction); Total Extinction Responses = the number of responses emitted during the extinction period; Responses per Reinforcement = the reinforcement-schedule requirement (e.g., FR value or mean ratio/interval responses per reinforcer) used to normalize extinction output across schedules. Orientation note: the numerator/denominator ordering is inferred on dimensional and conceptual grounds (the response-unit measure of Mowrer & Jones, 1945, expresses extinction in units of the schedule's required response cluster, i.e., total responses divided by responses-per-reinforcement). The surviving corrupted fragment's literal token order points the opposite way, and the 1960 JEAB scan could not be machine-read, so the orientation rests on theory rather than direct confirmation against the page.
followup_reason: Numerator/denominator orientation of the response-unit normalization is inferred from dimensional/conceptual grounds (Mowrer & Jones 1945 response-unit hypothesis) and runs counter to the corrupted fragment's literal token order. The 1960 JEAB source is a pre-1990 PMC scanned page image and is not machine-readable, so the orientation cannot be confirmed without consulting the physical/scanned paper.
editor_summary: Adjudicated index 122 (Bullock, 1960, JEAB 3:241-243), a brief note comparing repeated conditioning-extinction across reinforcement schedules. The original field held a single corrupted, concatenated fragment ("Response Units=Responses per Reinforcement Total Extinction Responses"). This is not a canonical EAB choice model (matching law, single-operant hyperbola, GML, signal-detection/bias, deVilliers); both reviewers and Editor 1 correctly treat it as a descriptive response-unit normalization (cf. Mowrer & Jones, 1945, response-unit hypothesis) with no recursive form. I adopt Editor 1's reconstructed static equation, Response Units = Total Extinction Responses / Responses per Reinforcement, which is the dimensionally sensible orientation that yields schedule-comparable units. Both reviews accept; Reviewer 2's substantive fix (make explicit that the orientation is inferred and that the fragment's literal order suggests the inverse) is well taken and folded into the definitions. Because the orientation rests on theory rather than verification against the non-machine-readable scan, I withhold full signoff (signoffs=0) and flag human follow-up against the physical paper. changed=true since the corrupted original was corrected.

final_static_definitions: S^{D} = number (or rate) of responses to the correct, matching stimulus key; S^{\Delta} = number (or rate) of responses to the incorrect, non-matching stimulus key. The Accuracy Ratio expresses matching responses as a proportion of total responses (the standard proportion-correct measure). The Error Ratio expresses incorrect responses relative to correct responses. Note: both expressions are reconstructions from corrupted OCR fragments of a scanned (non-machine-readable) 1960 JEAB matching-to-sample paper, not a quantitative matching-law study; no canonical EAB model (Herrnstein/Baum/Davison-Tustin) applies. The numerator/denominator orientation of the Error Ratio is inferred on semantic grounds and is unverified: viable alternatives include S^{D}/S^{\Delta} (literal token order) and S^{\Delta}/(S^{D}+S^{\Delta}) (proportion of errors). These may be extraction-tool artifacts rather than formally displayed equations in the original.
followup_reason: Correctness depends on the scanned (non-machine-readable) page images of Ferster (1960), PMC1404017, which neither editor nor reviewers could read. Both expressions are semantic reconstructions from corrupted OCR fragments; the Error Ratio numerator/denominator orientation is ambiguous (S^Delta/S^D vs S^D/S^Delta vs S^Delta/(S^D+S^Delta)), and these may be extraction artifacts rather than displayed equations. Verification requires inspecting the physical/scanned paper.
editor_summary: Both reviewers reached accept_with_changes, agreeing Editor 1 correctly declined to impose any canonical matching-law/SDT model on this 1960 matching-to-sample procedural paper and reconstructed two non-canonical response ratios honestly with low confidence. I adopt Editor 1's reconstructions: Accuracy Ratio = S^D/(S^D+S^Delta) (the only coherent proportion-correct reading) and Error Ratio = S^Delta/S^D (semantically preferred). Per both reviewers' fixes, I strengthened the definitions to explicitly flag the unverified directionality of the Error Ratio and list the competing forms, and to note these may be OCR/extraction artifacts. Final differs from the corrupted original, so changed=true. Because the source is an unreadable scan and the Error Ratio orientation cannot be confirmed, signoffs=0 and human_followup_required=true.

final_static_definitions: \bar{F}_{S^{\Delta}} = mean response force emitted in the presence of the negative/extinction stimulus S^{\Delta}; \bar{F}_{S^{D}} = mean response force emitted in the presence of the positive discriminative stimulus S^{D}. The inequality expresses the empirical finding that mean response force was greater during S^{\Delta} than during S^{D}. NOTE: the inequality direction and the supplied left-hand F are reconstructed from a transposed/corrupted fragment and EAB conventions, not confirmed against the (non-machine-readable, scanned) source; the reverse ordering \bar{F}_{S^{D}} > \bar{F}_{S^{\Delta}} cannot be excluded.

final_static_definitions: \text{Pre-tone } R = \text{operant response rate (responses per unit time) during the pre-tone baseline period}; \text{Tone } R = \text{operant response rate during the tone (CS) period}. This proportion-of-baseline suppression index runs from 0 (no suppression, Tone } R = \text{Pre-tone } R\text{) to 1 (complete suppression, Tone } R = 0\text{). NOTE: the original is a non-machine-readable scanned page image, so the exact orientation Carlton used could not be confirmed; the bounded subtractive form is given as the most defensible reconstruction. The dominant period alternative is the Annau & Kamin (1961) form } \frac{\text{Tone } R}{\text{Pre-tone } R + \text{Tone } R}\text{, which ranges from 0.5 (no suppression) to 0 (complete) and remains possible here.}
followup_reason: The exact suppression-ratio orientation cannot be verified because Carlton (1961, JEAB 4:379-381) survives only as a non-machine-readable scanned page image (PMC1404129). Editor 1's literal fragment reading is pathological (diverges at no-suppression), and both reviewers agree it reflects a likely numerator/denominator swap during extraction. The corrected bounded form (Pre-tone R - Tone R)/Pre-tone R is the most defensible reconstruction, but the Annau & Kamin (1961) B/(A+B) form is also plausible. A human must check the physical/scanned paper to confirm which metric Carlton actually printed.
editor_summary: Both independent reviewers (accept_with_changes; confidence 0.7 and 0.6) agreed the editor's literal corrected form, Pre-tone R / (Pre-tone R - Tone R), is mathematically pathological and not a recognized conditioned-suppression metric, and that the surviving corrupted fragment is more consistent with a bounded difference-over-baseline ratio whose numerator and denominator were swapped during \frac extraction. I applied that fix, replacing the headline static equation with the bounded proportion-of-suppression form (Pre-tone R - Tone R)/Pre-tone R (0 = none, 1 = complete) and recording the Annau & Kamin (1961) B/(A+B) alternative in the definitions. Static-only entry; the single-fragment, empty-recursive treatment is correct for this 3-page note. Withheld signoff (signoffs = 0) and flagged human follow-up because the exact metric depends on a scanned page image that none of us could read; the title typos (REIANFORCEMENT, DEPRIVATIONAND) are inherited from source metadata, not introduced.

final_static_definitions: N = cumulative amount (number of food units / reinforcers) ingested during the satiation session at elapsed time t; K = proportionality (intake-rate) constant; t = elapsed eating time since onset of the satiation session; n = shape exponent (n = 1 yields the linear special case N = Kt, i.e., a straight-line cumulative-intake curve at constant rate K, which is the form the paper's data predominantly support; n < 1 would give the negatively accelerated curvilinear form Skinner reported for rats but Reese & Hogenson did NOT find in pigeons). Reconstructed from the corrupted fragment "N=Ktn,"; NOT read from the scanned original. Competing candidate: the printed relation may have been the simple linear N = Kt, with the trailing "n" an OCR/subscript artifact rather than a free exponent, since the authors classified curve shapes descriptively (~64% straight with abrupt stop) rather than fitting a power law. Variable identity (amount eaten vs. responses) is reconstructed, not confirmed.
followup_reason: Source (PMC1404110) is a scanned-image 1962 JEAB paper with no machine-readable equations. The reconstructed power form N = K t^{n} cannot be distinguished from the simple linear N = Kt (with "n" a possible OCR/subscript artifact) without inspecting the physical/scanned page, and the paper's own finding of predominantly straight-line satiation curves makes the linear reading at least equally likely. Variable identity (cumulative grams eaten vs. pecks emitted) also needs confirmation against the scan.
editor_summary: Both reviewers returned accept_with_changes and agreed the reconstruction is honestly hedged with no fabricated citations or canonical models grafted on (correct, since this is a satiation paper, not a choice/matching paper). I retained N = K t^{n} as the primary reconstruction per Editor 1 and Reviewer 2, but applied both substantive reviewer fixes: (1) carried the competing linear candidate N = Kt into the equation-level definition rather than leaving it only in global notes, explicitly flagging that the linear special case (n=1) is what the data actually support; and (2) resolved the dependent-variable hedge toward cumulative amount/number of food units ingested per Reviewer 1, dropping the "pecking responses" alternative as unconfirmed. Recursive fields correctly left empty. Withholding signoff (signoffs=0) because the power-vs-linear form is unresolved and confirmable only against the scanned original; flagged for human follow-up.

final_recursive_definitions: Unverifiable fragment. The source (Sidman, 1962, JEAB 5(2):271-277) is available only as scanned page images; only the abstract is machine-readable. This is a procedural free-operant avoidance report, not a quantitative-modeling paper, and is unrelated to the matching-law / GML / signal-detection canon. The fragment matches no canonical EAB model and contains an undefined symbol z. It is also mislabeled "recursive": it is a closed-form expression linear in n with no T_{n-1} dependence, hence not a true recurrence. If taken at face value, n would index successive lever presses and the "5" would reflect the 5 s of accrued "safe time" per press confirmed in the abstract, but no such displayed equation could be verified in the source. Retained as a traceability echo only, at very low confidence; do not treat as a validated model.
followup_reason: Correctness cannot be confirmed: the paper exists only as scanned page images (not machine-readable), so the fragment T_n = 5n - z + 5 cannot be validated against the displayed text. It is unclear whether the paper contains any genuine displayed equation at all, the symbol z is undefined in available text, and the "recursive" role tag is mathematically inaccurate. editor_summary: Both reviewers accepted Editor 1's disposition, and I concur. final_static_definitions: M\theta_1 = the value of \theta_1 that yields the maximum visual cue (maximum angular difference) for a given rate change (a single symbol, not the product of M and \theta_1); \theta_1 = angle of the cumulative response curve representing the initial (first) response rate R_1; \theta_2 = angle representing the second response rate R_2; R_1 = initial (first) response rate; R_2 = second response rate; \arcsin\sqrt{R_1/(R_1+R_2)} = arcsine-square-root (angular, variance-stabilizing) transformation of the proportion of responding R_1/(R_1+R_2)
followup_reason: The arcsin argument was reconstructed from the canonical derivation and the machine-readable PMC abstract (which confirms the LHS "M\theta_1 = arc sin [Formula]" verbatim but obscures the argument). The exact glyphs of the argument are only verifiable against the scanned 1965 page images, which were not machine-readable. A quick check against the physical scan would confirm the sqrt(R_1/(R_1+R_2)) form.
editor_summary: Adjudicated index 545 (Herrick, 1965, JEAB, cumulative response curves). The original static equation M\theta_1 = \arcsin(R_1 - R_2) had the correct LHS but a wrong argument, and the definitions mis-parsed M\theta_1 as a product. Editor 1 corrected it to M\theta_1 = \arcsin\sqrt{R_1/(R_1+R_2)}, the variance-stabilizing arcsine-square-root of the proportion; Reviewer 2 independently derived the same result (tan theta = kR; maximizing theta_1 - theta_2 gives k = 1/sqrt(R_1 R_2), so sin(M\theta_1) = sqrt(R_1/(R_1+R_2))) and accepted, staking their name on it. Reviewer 1 returned null. The PMC abstract confirms the LHS verbatim and confirms theta_1/theta_2 represent rates R_1/R_2. I adopt Editor 1's correction with the clarified definitions (M\theta_1 as a single symbol). No recursive equation; the companion angular-difference cue existed in the paper but was not in the stored fields and was correctly not fabricated. Signing off (signoffs=1) given the strong derivation and confirmed LHS, while flagging human_followup_required=true because the obscured arcsin argument glyph is only fully verifiable against the scanned original.

final_static_definitions: C: the contact-protection (snubber) capacitance in microfarads (\mu\text{F}); R: the series snubber resistance in ohms (\Omega); I: the steady-state current through the contacts/load in amperes; E: the steady-state supply voltage (electromotive force) across the contacts in volts.
followup_reason: This is an out-of-canon apparatus/technical note on RC contact-protection (snubber) networks, not an EAB quantitative-behavior model, so the canonical models cannot anchor the reconstruction. The original 1965 JEAB paper is a scanned page image (Wiley/PMC serve only the abstract), so the displayed equations and their numeric constants could not be read machine-readably. The two design rules (C = I^2/10 microfarads; R = E/(10 I (1+50/E)) ohms) are reconstructed from the heavily corrupted fragment plus the standard relay snubber convention; the constants 10 and 50 and the (1+50/E) grouping match the C.C. Bates contact-protection formula, but that source is dated 1966 (one year AFTER this paper) and was not cited here, so faithfulness to THIS paper's exact form cannot be confirmed. Reviewers also materially disagreed on confidence (Reviewer 1 ~0.6, urging the constants be marked unverified; Reviewer 2 0.9 after external corroboration). Verification against the physical/scanned original is needed to confirm the exact constants and algebraic grouping.
editor_summary: Adjudicated catalog index 658, "A Transient Suppression Guide" (Riling & McDiarmid, JEAB 1965, 8(6):415-418). Both reviewers and Editor 1 agree this is an apparatus/technical note on RC contact-protection (snubber) networks for suppressing inductive transients across relay contacts, NOT an EAB quantitative-behavior model; the abstract confirms the topic. The EAB canon (matching law, GML, signal detection, hyperbola) does not apply, and the editor correctly did not force it. The garbled original fragment "C=12(in muF)RI(1+50)(in Omega)E" encodes two design rules, flagged by its two unit tags (microfarads, ohms). I adopt Editor 1's reconstruction: C = I^2/10 (microfarads) and R = E/(10 I (1+50/E)) (ohms), with the (1+50/E) factor in the denominator. Both LaTeX expressions compile cleanly and all four symbols are defined. final fields differ from the corrupted original, so changed = true. I sided with Reviewer 1's calibration over Reviewer 2's optimism on the signoff: the constants (10, 50) and grouping are reconstructed from the standard snubber convention and an external formula (Bates 1966, postdating and uncited by this 1965 paper), not confirmed against the non-machine-readable scan, and the two reviews materially disagreed on confidence. Therefore signoffs = 0 and human_followup_required = true pending verification against the physical/scanned original. Note: this overrides the existing data.json signoffs=1, which appears to be auto-flagged rather than equation-verified.

final_static_definitions: \mathrm{D.I.}: discrimination index; R^{S^{D}}: response rate in the presence of the reinforced stimulus (S^{D}); R^{S^{\Delta}}: response rate in the presence of the nonreinforced stimulus (S^{\Delta}). Note: the unweighted proportion is the canonical 1960s stimulus-control discrimination index; the stray coefficient 0.31 on the S^{\Delta} term in the source fragment is removed as an inferred extraction artifact, unverified against the scanned source (PMC1338182) and retained as a candidate datum if the scan is later OCR'd.
followup_reason: The load-bearing reconstruction step (removal of the 0.31 coefficient on the S^{\Delta} term) cannot be verified because Sadowsky (1966) is available only as scanned page images (PMC1338182, pp. 219-225) that are not machine-readable. The unweighted discrimination index is the canonical and most probable form, but the exact displayed equation and notation cannot be confirmed; the coefficient may have been a mis-spliced computed D.I. datum rather than pure injection noise. Confirm against the physical/OCR'd scan.
editor_summary: Both reviewers agree the reconstructed unweighted discrimination index, D.I. = R^{S^D}/(R^{S^D}+R^{S^\Delta}), is the canonical 1960s stimulus-control form and that the printed 0.31 coefficient on the S^{\Delta} term has no canonical basis (a discrimination ratio has unit weighting; it is not a fitted deVilliers-style bias/punishment parameter). Reviewer 1 accepts; Reviewer 2 accepts with the change that the coefficient removal be marked 'inferred, unverified against scan' rather than asserted as artifact, and that 0.31 be preserved as a candidate datum. I adopt Editor 1's equation and superscript fixes (SD -> S^{D}, SDelta -> S^{\Delta}) and apply Reviewer 2's wording fix in the definitions note. Reviewer 2's secondary point about subscript vs superscript notation for R is a minor non-error; I preserve the source fragment's superscript structure. Changed = true (coefficient removed, notation corrected). Signoffs = 0 because the load-bearing removal is unverifiable against the scanned source, warranting human follow-up.

final_static_definitions: X_i = value of the synthesized series X at sample index i (sampled at time t_i); t_i = time of the ith sample; \alpha_j = amplitude of the jth harmonic component; \omega_j = angular frequency of the jth harmonic component; \phi_j = (randomly varying) phase of the jth harmonic component
followup_reason: Source is a scanned page image and could not be machine-read, so the exact printed notation cannot be confirmed: in particular the upper summation limit (infinity vs a finite N or N/2 for the sampled IRT series) and whether the paper used an amplitude-phase single-cosine form versus a cosine-sine (a_n/b_n) pair. Verification requires sight of the physical/scanned 1966 JEAB original.
editor_summary: Both reviewers accept the reconstruction; the single displayed equation is a standard harmonic/Fourier-series decomposition of the IRT time series, which is the appropriate model for this 1966 spectral analysis of spaced (DRL) responding and correctly was NOT forced into a matching-law canon form. The LaTeX compiles and is internally consistent (amplitude alpha_j, angular frequency omega_j, random phase phi_j; outer sample index i, inner harmonic index j), with no sign/subscript/structural errors. I adopted the fix both reviewers converged on: rewording the prose definitions to drop the non-standard word "population" and to distinguish X_i (value at sample index i) from t_i (time of the ith sample), leaving the equation unchanged. The static equation LaTeX is therefore identical to the original, but the definitions changed, so changed=true. Because the upper summation limit and exact symbol choice cannot be confirmed against the scanned-only source, I withhold signoff (signoffs=0) and flag human followup against the physical paper.

final_static_definitions: R_1 = relative response rate to alternative 1; R_2 = relative response rate to alternative 2 (the left-side response symbol R is an editorial/reconstructed choice consistent with the Herrnstein-lineage JEAB convention; the exact symbol and whether Todorov printed the proportion form or the algebraically equivalent ratio form R_1/R_2 = (f_1/f_2)(m_1/m_2) cannot be confirmed from the scanned source); f_1, f_2 = frequency of reinforcement in schedules 1 and 2; m_1, m_2 = magnitude (duration of access to food) of reinforcement in schedules 1 and 2. The product f_i m_i is the relative reinforcement value, i.e., relative total access to food (the product of frequency and magnitude divided by the sum of products). Per the abstract, Todorov tested this unweighted value relation and found it held adequately only after frequency was weighted more heavily than magnitude (later expressed as greater sensitivity to reinforcement rate than to magnitude); the exact 1973 frequency-weighted functional form is not recoverable from the scan and is therefore not displayed.
followup_reason: Source (PMC1334140) is scanned page images; the left-side response symbol and whether Todorov printed the proportion or ratio surface form are reconstructed and can only be confirmed against the physical/scanned paper. The underlying concatenated/Herrnstein matching model with a frequency-times-magnitude value term is canonically certain, but the exact printed notation is unverified.
editor_summary: Adjudicated Editor 1 plus two accept-with-changes reviews. Accepted the core reconstruction: the stored right-hand-only fragment f_1 m_1/(f_1 m_1 + f_2 m_2) is correctly completed into the full concatenated/Herrnstein relative-matching relation. Applied the reviewers' agreed fix of standardizing the unconfirmed left-side symbol from P to R (relative response rate) and explicitly flagging it as editorial in the definitions field, not only the notes. Reframed the value relation in the definitions to reflect that this unweighted form was the hypothesis tested and largely disconfirmed (fit only after frequency was weighted more than magnitude), per the abstract. Upheld Editor 1's restraint in NOT fabricating the frequency-weighted/sensitivity form, which the scan does not expose. No recursive equation expected or present. Signed off (equation is canonically correct and faithful to the tested model) but flagged human followup because exact printed notation/surface form is only verifiable against the scanned original.

final_static_definitions: f_i: required number of pecks in the i-th 1-s subinterval; o_i: observed number of pecks in that subinterval; D: sum of squared deviations between required and obtained response-rate functions; Reinforcement delivered when deviation D is at or below the tolerance criterion C
followup_reason: The reconstructed criterion is a custom, method-specific shaping rule rather than a canonical EAB choice/matching/detection model, so it cannot be verified against any external canon. Source is a 1975 JEAB paper available only as scanned page images (not machine-readable). Substantive details that determine correctness, specifically whether the deviation measure is squared versus absolute, whether the upper index is exactly 5 subintervals, and the exact threshold notation C, can only be confirmed against the physical/scanned paper. editor_summary: Both reviewers issued accept verdicts and agreed the fragments were already clean, were faithfully preserved, and were correctly split into two static expressions (D = sum of squared deviations; D <= C) with no recursive equation present or implied. I concur and leave all final fields identical to the original, so changed=false. The equation lies outside the canonical EAB corpus (matching/GML/signal-detection), so there is no canon against which to verify structure; the reconstruction is internally coherent, algebraically valid, and the LaTeX compiles. I withhold signoff (signoffs=0) and flag human_followup_required=true because the remaining uncertainty is substantive rather than notational: whether the actual paper used squared versus absolute deviations and whether the index range was exactly i=1..5 can only be confirmed against the scanned 1975 page images, which are not machine-readable. Editor 1 honestly disclosed these limits and did not fabricate any source or citation.

final_static_definitions: W_1: reinforcement value of schedule-induced drinking (water) added to component 1, expressed in food-reinforcement-rate units; T_1, T_2: time allocated to schedule components 1 and 2; R_1, R_2: obtained rates of food reinforcement in components 1 and 2; P: proportion of time allocated to component 1, equated to the proportion of total reinforcement under the strict-matching premise with water value entering only component 1 (W_2 = 0). NOTE: the bridging matching identity P = (R_1 + W_1)/((R_1 + W_1) + R_2) is the load-bearing assumption used to solve for W_1; the equivalent simplified form is W_1 = (T_1/T_2) R_2 - R_1. The trailing (1-P) was reinterpreted from a printed subtracted product '- R(1-P)' into a denominator, and bare R was taken to be R_1 — both are inferences from model coherence and are NOT verified against the scanned 1975 page image. A competing literal reading (R = total rate, (1-P) as a multiplier) yields W_1 = (R_1 + R_2)(2P - 1) and cannot be excluded without the scan.
followup_reason: The reconstruction hinges on two unverifiable transcription inferences from a scanned (non-machine-readable) 1975 JEAB page image: (1) reinterpreting the fragment's subtracted product '- R(1-P)' as a division by (1-P), and (2) de-subscripting bare R to R_1. A canonically clean competing model, W_1 = (R_1+R_2)(2P-1), fits the literal fragment equally well, and both reviewers declined to confirm the specific printed form. Retrieve and read the physical/scanned page (PMC1333317) to disambiguate the ratio model from the difference model and to confirm whether Cohen expressed the relation in time (T) or reinforcement (R) terms.
editor_summary: Adopted Editor 1's Herrnstein time-allocation matching reconstruction as the most canonically coherent reading (numerator 'P R_1 + P R_2' matches the fragment exactly; passes the W_1=0 baseline reducing to P = R_1/(R_1+R_2)). Applied both reviewers' shared fix: surfaced the bridging matching identity P = (R_1+W_1)/((R_1+W_1)+R_2) as an explicit equation, and documented the simplified cross-check W_1 = (T_1/T_2)R_2 - R_1. Explicitly flagged the two non-literal, scan-unverifiable inferences (product-to-quotient and R->R_1) and the competing literal model W_1 = (R_1+R_2)(2P-1). Recursive fields correctly empty (static model only). Withheld signoff (signoffs=0) and set human_followup_required because correctness depends on details readable only from the scanned page and a structurally different competing model cannot be excluded.

final_static_definitions: R_1 = Response rate on lever 1; k = Constant; r_1, r_2 = Obtained reinforcement rate for each lever; p_1, p_2 = Obtained punishment rate for each lever; r_0 = Extraneous/background reinforcement rate (Herrnstein's r_e); \frac{R_1}{R_1 + R_2} = Relative rate of responding on lever 1
followup_reason: The relative-rate matching equation is the paper's signature result and is web-corroborated and canon-consistent (Deluty's additive/competitive-suppression punishment model), so it is high confidence. The absolute-rate companion form, specifically the background-reinforcement symbol r_0 (a non-canonical stand-in for Herrnstein's extraneous-reinforcement term r_e), could not be confirmed verbatim because the 1976 JEAB source is a scanned page image and not machine-readable. Recommend confirming the absolute-rate form and its symbol set against the physical/scanned original.
editor_summary: Adjudicated index 1785 (Deluty 1976). Both reviewers accept; Reviewer 2 requested only descriptive (non-LaTeX) changes. Kept both equations unchanged in LaTeX: they are canon-consistent and the absolute and relative forms reduce to one another (k and r_0 cancel). Applied definition cleanups: corrected R_1 to "response rate on lever 1" (Editor 1) and annotated r_0 as extraneous/background reinforcement (Herrnstein's r_e) per Reviewer 2. The imprecise "single-operant hyperbola" role label was a tag-level note, not part of the cataloged equation fields, so no LaTeX change was needed. Recursive fields correctly left empty (static-only paper). Signed off on equation correctness/faithfulness; flagged the r_0 symbol and verbatim absolute-rate form for scan verification since the 1976 source is non-machine-readable.

final_static_definitions: P_A = time allocation in component A (proportion/amount of session time spent in A; dependent-variable symbol reconstructed, original may use T_A or B_A); R_A, R_B = rate of reinforcement in component A/B; R_0 = rate of reinforcement from extraneous sources (Herrnstein's r_e; original may use r_e); K = scaling/asymptote constant (original may use lowercase k); m = dimensionless weight on alternate-component reinforcement indexing the degree of cross-component interaction
followup_reason: Source is a pre-1990 JEAB paper available on PMC only as scanned page images, so equations are not machine-readable and could not be corroborated. The structural form (Herrnstein 1970 multiple-schedule hyperbola applied to time allocation) is canonically secure, but exact published glyphs (K vs k, R_0 vs r_e, the dependent-variable symbol P_A vs T_A/B_A) and whether the paper contains additional equations beyond the single surviving fragment cannot be verified without the physical scan.
editor_summary: Both reviewers accepted the structural reconstruction; Reviewer 2 requested definitional fixes I adopted. The denominator-label typo 'R_)' -> 'R_0' is retained. I narrowed the P_A definition from the hedged 'rate of responding or time allocation' to time allocation (consistent with the paper's title and Baum tradition) and flagged the symbol as reconstructed. I removed the unsupported '(0-1)' bound on the interaction weight m, restating it as a dimensionless cross-component interaction weight, and annotated K and R_0 as reconstructed symbols (possible lowercase k / r_e). Equation body unchanged: P_A = K R_A/(R_A + m R_B + R_0). Recursive fields correctly empty. Definitions differ from the original, so changed=true. Withholding signoff (signoffs=0) and flagging human follow-up because exact glyphs and equation completeness are unverifiable against the non-machine-readable scan.

final_static_equation: \frac{P_1}{P_2} = \frac{R_1}{R_2}; \log\!\left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right) = a \,\log\!\left(\frac{R_1}{R_2}\right) + \log c; \frac{T_1}{T_2} = c \left( \frac{R_1}{R_2} \right)^{b}; P_1 = \frac{k \, R_1}{R_1 + R_2 + R_0}; P_1 = k' \left( \frac{R_1}{R_1 + R_2 + R_3 + R_0} \right)^{a}
final_static_definitions: P_1, P_2 = Responses on keys 1 and 2; R_1, R_2 = Reinforcers obtained on keys 1 and 2; c = bias parameter; a = sensitivity parameter (the choice/concurrent sensitivity slope in the log GML, eq 2; reused as the absolute-rate matching exponent in eq 5, per the paper's convention); T_1, T_2 = Time spent responding on keys 1 and 2; b = sensitivity parameter (time-allocation power form); k, k' = asymptotic/scaling constants for absolute response rate; R_0 = reinforcers maintaining other (extraneous/background) behavior, i.e. the r_e term in Herrnstein's hyperbola; R_3 = reinforcers on a third response key (the study arranged VI schedules singly and concurrently on one, two, and three keys; eq 4 is the two-alternative case and eq 5 the generalized three-key case)
followup_reason: Source is a 1976 JEAB scanned page-image (not machine-readable), so the exact internal structure of the two absolute-rate models cannot be confirmed against the original. Specifically: (1) the presence and exact role of the R_3 term in eq 5 (plausible given the documented one/two/three-key design but unverified), and (2) whether the matching exponent in eq 5 sits on the whole ratio as written, P=k'(R_1/sum)^a, versus on individual terms, P=k'R_1^a/(R_1^a+R_2^a+...), as Davison's generalized absolute-rate work is sometimes written. Both reviewers flagged these provenance points and one declined to stake their name on eq 5's R_3 term until the scan is checked. Equations are canonically consistent and faithful to the surviving fragments, but faithfulness of eq 5 requires verification against the physical paper.
editor_summary: Both independent reviewers returned accept_with_changes with no structural/math errors: all five equations are canonical members of the matching family (strict Herrnstein ratio matching; Baum 1974 log-form generalized matching; power-form GML for time allocation; concurrent extension of Herrnstein's single-operant hyperbola with extraneous-reinforcement term R_0; and a power/sensitivity generalization for absolute response rate). Editor 1's repairs (typo fixes 'sensitiviy'->'sensitivity', 'paramater'->'parameter'; adding missing definitions for R_0 and R_3) are conservative and correct, so final differs from the ORIGINAL (changed=true). I adopted the reviewers' non-structural clarifications into the definitions: relabeled eq 4 as the two-alternative concurrent hyperbola with R_0 as the r_e term, identified eq 5 as the generalized three-key case (consistent with the paper's documented singly/two/three-key design, which corroborates R_3 rather than treating it as an OCR artifact), and disambiguated the reused symbol 'a' between the eq-2 choice sensitivity and the eq-5 absolute-rate exponent. No equations were added or removed; recursive fields correctly remain empty. I withheld signoff (signoffs=0) and set human_followup_required=true because the scanned source prevents positive confirmation of eq 5's exact form (R_3 term and whole-ratio vs per-term exponent); reviewer confidence was 0.78 each and one reviewer explicitly would not vouch for eq 5's R_3 term until the scan is checked.

final_static_equation: P_1 = k \cdot \frac{R_1}{R_1 + R_2 + R_e}; P(A) = \frac{p_r(A)}{p_r(A) + p_r(D)}; \frac{v(A)}{v(A) + v(C)} = \frac{a}{a + c}

followup_reason: Source is a 1976 JEAB scanned page image (not machine-readable), so equations were reconstructed from the EAB canon using corrupted fragments. Eq3 was repaired from an invalid ratio=proportion form to the proportion form v(A)/(v(A)+v(C)) = a/(a+c) to parallel Eq2, but the choice between this and the pure-ratio form v(A)/v(C) = a/c cannot be confirmed without the original. The cross-equation alternative labels (A/D in Eq2 vs A/C in Eq3) also could not be reconciled against the scan. Both reviewers gave accept_with_changes at ~0.6 confidence; verification of Eq3's form and the network-node labeling requires checking the physical/scanned paper.
editor_summary: Adjudicated Editor 1's corrected_partial reconstruction against two accept_with_changes reviews. Kept Eq1 (multi-alternative Herrnstein hyperbola, P_1 = kR_1/(R_1+R_2+R_e)) and Eq2 (probability-matching, P(A) = p_r(A)/(p_r(A)+p_r(D)) with the well-justified LHS extraction-artifact repair) as canonically sound. Applied the fix both reviewers requested: repaired Eq3 from the malformed ratio=proportion form v(A)/v(C)=a/(a+c) to the internally consistent proportion form v(A)/(v(A)+v(C))=a/(a+c), which parallels Eq2's structure. Final fields differ from the original (Eq2 LHS and Eq3), so changed=true. No recursive equation present in fragments; empty recursive fields retained. Withheld signoff (signoffs=0) and flagged human_followup_required because the Eq3 form choice and the A/C/D node labels depend on the non-machine-readable 1976 scan and could not be confirmed.

final_static_definitions: R = Local response rate; T = Time since onset of interval; a = Rate-scaling parameter; k = Slope parameter

R = a T^{k} is a generic two-parameter power function, not a named canonical EAB model, and both reviewers flagged a live alternative interpretation: Lund's stated 'quantitative indices of the temporal pattern of response' may instead denote an index-of-curvature measure rather than a power law of local rate vs. time. The equation text has no detectable algebraic/notation error and is retained verbatim, but its identity and definitions require confirmation against the physical/scanned paper.
editor_summary: Both independent reviewers and Editor 1 agree the single fragment R = a T^{k} is clean LaTeX, internally consistent, free of corruption artifacts, and maps one-to-one to one displayed equation with no recursive form indicated. There is no canonical EAB model to correct it against and no detectable sign/term error in a monomial, so the equation text stands unchanged and no field differs from the original (changed = false). However, the panel cannot sign off: the scanned-image source is unverifiable, the variable definitions are an interpretive reconstruction from the paper's title/topic rather than read from the scan, and a credible alternative (an index-of-curvature measure) is consistent with the abstract's wording. Confidence held at ~0.55; signoffs = 0 and human follow-up flagged pending verification against the physical paper.

final_static_definitions: Y = Dependent measure; X = Independent measure; a = Slope; b = Intercept

The equation form itself (generic straight-line regression) and the corrected intercept symbol are sound.
editor_summary: Both reviewers accept and I concur. This is a DRL key-peck vs. treadle-press operant-comparison (methodological) study, not a quantitative-law paper, so no canonical EAB model (Herrnstein matching/hyperbola, Baum GML, deVilliers punishment, Davison-Tustin/McCarthy-Davison signal detection) applies; Editor 1 correctly declined to retrofit one. The only correction is in the definitions: the OCR-extracted intercept symbol "n = intercept" was fixed to "b = Intercept" to match the literal "b" in the equation. This makes changed = true.
